speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to begin our evaluation, have you noticed if these symptoms started suddenly or developed gradually over time? Additionally, has this issue occurred before or does it radiate from your neck?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of anabolic steroid use, diabetes, and chronic alcohol consumption, I need to determine if this is a compressive neuropathy or a metabolic issue. Have you noticed any specific neck pain or muscle wasting in the right arm, and do you experience any numbness in your hands?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel, Liver_Function_Tests.
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Cervical_Spine.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor) causing right-sided Pancoast syndrome.

The combination of progressive right arm weakness, sensory loss, burning pain, significant weight loss, and your history of heavy smoking makes a lung apex tumor compressing the brachial plexus the most likely diagnosis, rather than Multiple Sclerosis.

I have already requested an MRI of your cervical spine; please await the results while we consider a Chest CT to visualize the lung apex.
